OpenAI 发布 GPT-6 Sol 和 GPT-6 Luna：旗舰级能力下放，API 价格砍半

OpenAI 推出 GPT-6 家族的两款新模型 Sol 和 Luna，主打“接近旗舰的能力，大幅更低的价格”。API 价格比上一代 GPT-5.6 的促销价再降 50%。

先理清命名。本月早些时候，OpenAI 发布了 GPT-6 Astra，定位是最强的旗舰模型。这次的 Sol 是中档，Luna 是轻量档，相当于同一代技术的“大、中、小杯”。三款模型用相似的方法训练，所以 Astra 在编程、事实准确性、操作电脑等方面的进步，也带到了更便宜的两款上。

OpenAI 这次的对比对象主要是 Anthropic 的 Claude。以下数据都来自 OpenAI 自己公布的评测，第三方复现结果还需等待。

在模拟跨应用处理销售、财务、HR 等业务流程的 AutomationBench 上，Sol 以最高推理强度拿到 33.2%，每个任务成本约 0.27 美元。它超过了最高强度的 Claude Opus 5（26.9%），成本只有后者的 9% 左右，也略高于低强度的 Astra。“推理强度”可以理解为让模型想多久，想得越久，效果越好，但也越贵。

编程方面，在真实代码库的长任务评测 DeepSWE 上，Sol 得分 68.8%，和 Claude Fable 5 的 69.9% 只差 1.1 个百分点，每任务成本低约 80%。更便宜的 Luna 也有 66.6%，与中等强度的 Opus 5、Fable 5 相当，成本低 93% 到 96%。在让 AI 操作电脑完成任务的 OSWorld 2.0 上，Sol 和 Opus 5 分数几乎打平，成本同样低约 80%。

对开发者来说，这意味着跑长时间的编程 AI 智能体会便宜很多。OpenAI 透露，内部研究员每天的 token 消耗按 API 价格算，中位数超过 600 美元。模型越能干，这笔账就越重要。

另一个实用改进是提示缓存。简单说，你反复发送的相同内容，比如系统提示、整个代码库，第二次读取时可以打一折，也就是缓存输入享受 90% 折扣。现在中途调整推理强度或开关工具都不会让缓存失效，开发者还能自己指定缓存的断点。GitHub 表示，这些改进让 Copilot 需要重新处理的 token 减少了一半以上，响应也更快。

使用体验上，Sol 和 Luna 继承了 Astra 的回答风格：更直接，术语更少，废话更少，回答略短。在事实准确性上，OpenAI 称 Sol 的错误比上一代少了约一半。

可用情况：即日起，Plus、Pro、Business、Enterprise 和 Edu 用户可以在 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 中使用这两款模型。免费用户和 Go 用户可以在桌面端用 Luna。普通 Chat 界面暂未上线，ChatGPT 端会在当天分批推送。API 模型名为 gpt-6-sol 和 gpt-6-luna。

"I was talking to Dan Boneh, who is a great professor of computer science and cryptography at Stanford. His take on AI was: You have two choices. You can ban it, and by the way, that won't work. Or you can make the problems so hard that you can't solve them without AI."

"What he's seeing is, 'I've got students solving things that no student in history could have ever solved.' That's what's possible. text:
Ben Horowitz on why a16z is incubating The Horowitz Andreessen Academy: the Industrial Revolution remade education. AI will too.

"The university system started out as a religious institution with the Jesuits and so forth. Then the Industrial Revolution came, and all of a sudden everybody needed a higher level of the ability to learn things, the ability to be literate."

"The university system exploded in the US. The universities got much bigger, and there became many more of them."

"That was really necessary to train the population to enter the corporate world. It's hard for people to understand now, but in 1700 there was no corporate world. There was a farm world, and then all of a sudden we get these companies."

"To exist in that environment, you've got to be able to read and write and do math... To a large extent, the America that we have was built on the backs of our great universities."

"We're hitting the AI revolution now, which is going to be, in our estimation, as transformational in terms of jobs, the way jobs are done, and the kinds of jobs that are available, as the Industrial Revolution was to the agricultural society that came before it."

"The idea that the training for the Industrial Revolution is going to map into the AI revolution, probably not perfectly. There needs to be a pioneer that shows the way: How do you train somebody into the new world?"

@bhorowitz

prompt 👇

Prompt: Create abhigh-end design poster from this photo. 

Use a 3:4 vertical composition overall, divided into two equal sections with a strict 1:1 height ratio, each occupying 50% of the image.

Top half: Preserve the original photo, maintaining the subject’s identity, structure, posture, realistic texture, natural lighting and shadows, and original color atmosphere. Only apply subtle, refined color grading to give it the quality of an art magazine or exhibition image. To fit the format, the surrounding environment may be naturally extended if needed, but the subject must not be stretched, distorted, or altered.

Bottom half: Extract only the most recognizable subject, contour, structure, posture, and narrative relationship from the photo, and reconstruct them into a centrally composed torn-paper cutout digital collage. Do not fully copy the original photo, do not redraw every object, and do not preserve most of the background. Remove irrelevant details proactively, keeping only the structures, directional flow, and visual memory points that best represent the original subject.

The bottom half must use a centered composition: place a vertical, irregular torn crack in the center of a large light-colored fiber paper background. The crack should have realistic rough edges and thickness, and it must serve as the core visual focus of the composition.

The content inside the crack should not be a realistic scene. Instead, reconstruct the subject using simplified geometric color blocks, reduced contours, and layered collage elements, creating a more restrained, abstract reorganization that is still instantly recognizable. If necessary, key parts may slightly break through the edge of the tear and extend outward to create tension and a sense of emerging from the surface, while still keeping the overall result restrained.

Even if the original image has a weak composition, a messy background, or a small subject, you should actively make new artistic judgments—rescuing it into a strong finished work through reduction, reorganization, cropping, scale adjustments, and whitespace. Truly re-direct the image rather than simply copying the original.

The composition must preserve a very large amount of intentional negative space. This negative space should not feel like empty background, but should work together with the central tear, the internal color-block subject, and a few supporting elements to create breathing room, spatial rhythm, and pause. Prefer less rather than more. Build a refined visual order through the central tear and a small number of high-value graphic elements.

Emphasize a paper-craft material quality: preserve the paper texture, fibers, rough edges, curling, layered thickness, and soft shadows, so that both the tear and the paper surface feel real and tactile. The overall result should be a high-end digital collage, not a photograph of a handmade craft piece. Avoid smooth vector graphics, cheap-looking 3D, photographic filters, and overly realistic rendering.

For the color palette, extract 2–4 of the most elegant and vivid colors from the top photo and reinterpret them. The overall palette should remain light, airy, restrained, and refined. Use large areas of warm white, off-white, and pale gray-white as the main paper colors, and reconstruct the subject inside the tear using a small number of brightened, purified, and de-muddied composite color blocks. Avoid dirty grays, aged-looking tones, visual clutter, and cheap high saturation.
